context: The Mirai Botnet: A Wake-Up Call for IoT. In 2016, the Mirai botnet infected thousands of IoT devices, including routers and security cameras. It exploited weak, factory-default passwords to gain unauthorized access at massive scale. Researchers later traced the origin of the attack to several university networks. 2016. Year of the attack. Attack Vector is Weak default passwords, Percentage is 62%. Attack Vector is Unpatched firmware, Percentage is 28%. This case study covers the. Mirai botnet attack applied to. IoT devices. Lecturers should emphasize the role of weak default credentials and the scale of the resulting. DDoS attacks.
